name: DJI RS 4
about: Joint axes, offsets and boxes for the sandbox's Gimbal object. Lengths in mm, in the HANDLE's frame (the Gimbal object's mount) with all joints at 0: handle along z, hand end up (+z), camera end down; the camera looks along +x (front); +y is the camera's left. DJI publishes no CAD or axis dimensions for the RS 4: the numbers below are estimates from its overall size (370 x 191 x 189 mm unfolded) and must be measured on the real gimbal. A balanced gimbal has all three axes through the camera's centre of gravity, so 'point' is the same for each joint; only the axis directions (J2's tilt in particular) and the camera centre's distance below the pan motor change where the camera points. Copy this file to make a model for another gimbal or rig; the Gimbal object picks it by file name.

joints.name: J2
joints.about: roll motor, behind the camera. Not at right angles to J1: tilted 56.4 deg from the lens line towards the hand end (34 deg from the handle axis), fitted to two level-camera readings with J1, J2 near 180 (hand end up: J 173.5 / -179.0 / -69.4, world pitch -2.2, roll 1.2; J 178.1 / -178.8 / -71.1). Square to J1 would be [1, 0, 0].

joints.name: J3
joints.about: tilt motor, beside the camera; +J3 tilts the lens towards the hand end, -90 looks down the handle

camera.about: camera centre (on all three axes when balanced) and its lens and right directions at home. No camera body is drawn: the Gimbal's Camera object sits here.
